subject: Lighting Labs — temporary quota buffer & proration plan
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@lightinglabs.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick: launch traffic spike — temporary quota bump?

Jonas,

We’re going live with the feature flag rollout tomorrow at 13:00 PDT and our telemetry shows we may peak at ~3x the usual QPS for a 36–48 hour window. That will blow past our current quota and we’ll start returning 429s unless we get short-term headroom.

Can Redwood provision a temporary increase to our rate limit and quota for ~72 hours? Also need to understand the billing treatment — if we exceed our cap, is there a way to 1) get a one-off credit on overrun charges, or 2) accept a short-term blended rate so we don’t get hit with sticker overrun pricing for a one-time launch? I attached a quick billing snapshot that shows our baseline and projected uplift.

Attached: LightingLabs_billing_snapshot_Q2.xlsx

I can loop in Accounting if you need a PO.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product
Lighting Labs

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@lightinglabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: launch traffic spike — temporary quota bump?

Thanks for the heads up, Samira — and thanks for the snapshot. Looping Ben (billing/ops) and Laura (contract/procurement path) so we can move quickly.

High level we can do a provisional uplift for a fixed short window and then true-up on the next invoice. Two ways to handle billing:
- Provisional uplift with a blended per-token rate for the uplift window (simpler for invoicing).
- Keep overrun at standard overrun rates but apply a predefined one-time credit against the overrun invoice (requires PO/approval).

If you can confirm the approximate uplift factor (x2/x3) and the intended window (start/end), we’ll propose a numeric option. We have limited spare headroom in the us-west pool but can reserve capacity if you confirm within the hour.

Ben/Laura — I’d like a short doc with 1) the uplift ceiling we can commit to for 72 hours, 2) a blended uplift rate option, and 3) the credit path if Lighting Labs provides a PO/commit. Goal: let them launch without 429s and avoid sticker shock on billing.

Jonas
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.k@lightinglabs.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: launch traffic spike — temporary quota bump? (proposal)

Samira / Team,

We can execute a short-term uplift. Proposed terms below (designed to be fast to approve):

1) Window: 2027-05-08 12:00 PDT through 2027-05-11 12:00 PDT (72 hours).
2) Ceiling: 3x nominal QPS up to 250k generated tokens/hour (whichever is lower).
3) Billing treatment (choose A or B):
   A) Blended uplift: During the 72h window, all extra consumption above baseline billed at a blended uplift rate of $0.0030 per generated token (prorated to actual minutes). No additional credits.
   B) Standard overrun + conditional credit: Extra consumption billed at standard overrun rate $0.0045 per token; Lighting Labs receives a one-time credit equal to 25% of the overrun invoice for that window if they provide a PO referencing deal LL-2027-042 and prepay 50% of the estimated uplift amount within 3 business days. Credit applies to the first subsequent invoice only.
4) Cancellation: If you do not use the uplift in the window, there is no charge.

Notes: Option A gives predictability and is faster to sign off (we can action on email approval). Option B preserves standard pricing but gives you upside via credit if accounting can handle the prepay.

Please indicate which option Lighting Labs prefers and whether Accounting can issue a PO (send to invoices@lightinglabs.ai). If you want we can also convert this to a one-page amendment and route it through DocuSign.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@lightinglabs.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: launch traffic spike — temporary quota bump? (procurement note)

Couple of procurement items to flag so Accounting can process quickly if you go with Option B (prepay + credit):
- PO language should reference: "Temporary uplift window and one-time overrun credit — deal LL-2027-042".
- Prepay invoice will include an estimate. We’ll true-up against actuals on the next invoice and apply the credit there.
- Credit will be limited to the first billing period after the uplift and cannot be carried forward.

If you pick Option A, email approval from an authorized Lighting Labs contact is sufficient; we’ll add a short amendment note to the customer record for audit.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@lightinglabs.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounting <invoices@lightinglabs.ai>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@lightinglabs.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: launch traffic spike — temporary quota bump? (acceptance)

Thanks, team — and apologies for the slow reply. Accounting reviewed both options and we’ll take Option B (standard overrun + conditional credit). They can prepay 50% of the estimate immediately once you send the prepay invoice. PO attached and PO number is LL-PO-5567.

Attached: LL_PO_5567.pdf

We understand credit will apply only to the first invoice after the uplift and that the uplift window is the 72-hour period you proposed. Please send the prepay invoice to invoices@lightinglabs.ai and confirm when the provisional uplift has been reserved so we can flip the flag.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, Lighting Labs
